head_commit.message: [Issue #8103] Restructure logging/metrics for workflow service (#9085) ## Summary Fixes #8103 ## Changes proposed * Rework / reconfigure the workflow management logging/metrics * Changed some logic in the SQS parsing to make it easier to link SQS messages to underlying events (created an SQS Container) * Had to rework all the tests that interact with the event handler to use the new SQS container - no meaningful changes * Adjusted the main loop to no longer sleep - the sqs polling waits 10 seconds now, so the sleep isn't needed ## Context for reviewers This is mostly just cleaning up logging and adding a few in places that were missing it. I ran things locally and just kept adjusting it when it felt like there was too much/too little info for a given event. The biggest change by far is making the SqsMessageContainer class. I wanted to pass in a metric context to the event handler and reworking it again to pass another field down convinced me that we should instead do this approach. That way the event handler input doesn't need to change if we add more later - we can just add it to this class. Made it so the process tracks a few different useful metrics: * Duration of processing request (one for just event handling, one factoring in SQS queue time) * Error classes clearly separated out * More consistent info on each log * An obvious message to check against for metrics / "what happened" for a given workflow ## Validation steps You'll need the API running locally, and also want to run the workflow service with `make cmd args="workflow workflow-main"`. To send events, go to http://localhost:8080/docs#/Workflow/put_v1_workflows_events - you can use the TODO Api User Key for sending events. You'll need to find an opportunity in your DB, you can then send workflow events against that opportunity with (swapping in the appropriate ID): ```py { "event_type": "start_workflow", "metadata": {}, "start_workflow_context": { "entity_id": "717b8d3a-f4a5-4d45-854a-607ae6aed554", "entity_type": "opportunity", "workflow_type": "initial_prototype" } } ``` If your service is running, it'll immediately consume the events - for me locally these events take maybe 20ms to get processed from sending them. head_commit.message: [Issue #8103] Restructure logging/metrics for workflow service (#9085) ## Summary Fixes #8103 ## Changes proposed * Rework / reconfigure the workflow management logging/metrics * Changed some logic in the SQS parsing to make it easier to link SQS messages to underlying events (created an SQS Container) * Had to rework all the tests that interact with the event handler to use the new SQS container - no meaningful changes * Adjusted the main loop to no longer sleep - the sqs polling waits 10 seconds now, so the sleep isn't needed ## Context for reviewers This is mostly just cleaning up logging and adding a few in places that were missing it. I ran things locally and just kept adjusting it when it felt like there was too much/too little info for a given event. The biggest change by far is making the SqsMessageContainer class. I wanted to pass in a metric context to the event handler and reworking it again to pass another field down convinced me that we should instead do this approach. That way the event handler input doesn't need to change if we add more later - we can just add it to this class. Made it so the process tracks a few different useful metrics: * Duration of processing request (one for just event handling, one factoring in SQS queue time) * Error classes clearly separated out * More consistent info on each log * An obvious message to check against for metrics / "what happened" for a given workflow ## Validation steps You'll need the API running locally, and also want to run the workflow service with `make cmd args="workflow workflow-main"`. To send events, go to http://localhost:8080/docs#/Workflow/put_v1_workflows_events - you can use the TODO Api User Key for sending events. You'll need to find an opportunity in your DB, you can then send workflow events against that opportunity with (swapping in the appropriate ID): ```py { "event_type": "start_workflow", "metadata": {}, "start_workflow_context": { "entity_id": "717b8d3a-f4a5-4d45-854a-607ae6aed554", "entity_type": "opportunity", "workflow_type": "initial_prototype" } } ``` If your service is running, it'll immediately consume the events - for me locally these events take maybe 20ms to get processed from sending them.
